messages:
maria (marketing): Hey team — draft benchmark narrative attached in the doc. Need quick agreement on the latency vs cost story for the launch post + webinar. Thoughts?

sam (growth): skimming — love the high-level. we should call out p95 latency and $/1M tokens side-by-side. marketers like a clear dollar number. :money_with_wings:

alex (product): agree. also add a ‘real-world SLO’ line: 200ms p95 for chat vs 500ms for long-context generation. makes the tradeoff concrete.

jess (data): +1. For charts: use median + p95 for latency; cost as $/1M tokens on a secondary axis. maybe log-scale for cost if we span quantized vs fp16.

noah (design): For visuals I can do two panels: left = latency curves (median/p95) across models, right = scatter cost vs p95 with size = throughput. clean legend, muted palette.

maria (marketing): Good. Messaging note: position Redwood as "predictable latency at significantly lower unit cost" — avoid hyperbole like "cheapest". Focus on controls (batching, cache, routing) that enable that.

sam (growth): Also call out the Dedicated offer: "reserved capacity for predictable throughput". That’s a conversion hook in webinars.

jess (data): Chart data notes (raw):
```
model,median_ms,p95_ms,cost_per_1M
redwood-v1,60,140,120
redwood-v1-quant,80,180,48
open-llm,90,240,200
```
use these as placeholder numbers for now.

alex (product): For the narrative flow: 1) problem statement (latency/cost unpredictability) 2) benchmark setup & workload (chat vs batch embeddings) 3) results + actionable levers (what we changed: batching, quant, routing) 4) customer outcomes + CTA.

noah (design): Question: should the cost axis be $/1M tokens or $/hour for Dedicated? mixing units in one slide can confuse.

jess (data): Keep charts per-unit ($/1M) for public blog; have a separate slide/table in the webinar for Dedicated pricing ($/hour + reserved). Callouts work.

maria (marketing): Copy idea for lead capture: "See live demo + customer workload estimate — reserve your slot". Capture webinar signups into SFDC with lead score if they choose Dedicated. @sam can you confirm routing?

sam (growth): Routing plan: webinar signups -> MQL in HubSpot -> if they select "enterprise" checkbox, create high-priority lead, assign to AE queue; otherwise send to nurturing drip + trial enablement. I’ll drop the flow in the doc.

alex (product): One more: include an A/B blurb in the post on how routing fallback works when the primary model is saturated — shows resilience. short paragraph.

maria (marketing): Nice. Timeline: draft blog and charts by Fri, review on Mon, webinar deck ready Wed, dry-run Thu. Is that realistic?

jess (data): I can have cleaned CSV + chart exports by Thu morning.

noah (design): I’ll deliver PNG + slide assets by Wed EOD.

sam (growth): I’ll wire up signup form + HubSpot mapping by Wed.

maria (marketing): Action items:
- jess: finalize numbers & export charts (due Thu)
- noah: visuals for blog + webinar (due Wed)
- sam: signup + routing (due Wed)
- alex: write the product callouts paragraph (due Fri)
- maria: synthesize post copy + webinar outline (due Fri)

chartbot: Chart generation kicked: plotting latency curves and cost scatter. Output path: /tmp/bench/1749001234/plots.zip

maria (marketing): Perfect. Small copy note: use plain language for latency — e.g., "~140ms p95" instead of too many decimal places.

jess (data): OK final thought on the axis: add a vertical band highlighting our target SLO range on latency charts (shaded green). simple and effective.

maria (marketing): Love it. If no major objections, I’ll finalize the narrative and schedule a 30m review Mon 10am PT. :calendar:
